s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and abdominal pain in the context of marked weight loss and dehydration
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Marked gastric distension on abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs
Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta on CT
Marked leanness due to a month of religious fasting

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and abdominal pain in the context of marked weight loss and dehydration
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Marked gastric distension on abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs
Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta on CT
Marked leanness due to a month of religious fasting

differentials: Intra-abdominal desmoplastic small round cell tumor
per_call: Intra-abdominal desmoplastic small round cell tumor

shortlist.label: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta on CT, consistent with patient's symptoms and marked leanness

shortlist.label: Gastric outlet obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Intractable vomiting and abdominal distension, although no intrinsic luminal lesions were found on endoscopy

shortlist.label: Vascular compression
shortlist.why_kept: CT findings demonstrating duodenal compression, supporting this diagnosis as a possible cause of symptoms

shortlist.label: Wilkie syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, similar to Superior mesenteric artery syndrome, but less common

shortlist.label: Median arcuate ligament syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of abdominal pain and vomiting due to compression of the celiac artery, although less directly related to the patient's specific symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with marked gastric distension and compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta on CT, are consistent with superior mesenteric artery syndrome. The patient's marked leanness due to a month of religious fasting likely contributed to the reduced aortomesenteric angle, supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gastric outlet obstruction
rejected.why: Normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy ruled out intrinsic luminal lesions

rejected.label: Vascular compression
rejected.why: This is a broader term that is encompassed by the more specific diagnosis of superior mesenteric artery syndrome

rejected.label: Wilkie syndrome
rejected.why: This is another term for superior mesenteric artery syndrome, but the provided CT findings and clinical presentation more directly support the chosen diagnosis

rejected.label: Median arcuate ligament syndrome
rejected.why: The CT findings specifically mention compression between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, not the median arcuate ligament
